steps: Identify statutory requirements for employment in service: §14 requires Estonian citizenship, at least secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency; §15 lists disqualifying circumstances (criminal convictions, court-deprived rights, prohibited close-family relations, other statutory preclusions).

Check authoritative registry data: population registry shows ee_citizen=true and full_capacity=true, education registry shows secondary_education=true, language registry shows speaks_estonian=true, criminal-records registry shows criminal_conviction=false.
Verify applicant's sworn statements about no family conflict with supervising official — no registry contradictions and applicant's statement aligns with §15(4) nepotism restriction absence.
No registry or case facts indicate other statutory preclusions (court deprivation of right to work, special-post restrictions) or the need for further qualifications for an unspecified post.
Conclude that the statutory conditions of §14 are satisfied and none of the disqualifications in §15 are present on the provided information, so employment as an official is permitted.
justification.text: All statutory eligibility conditions of §14 are met per authoritative registers (Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency) and no disqualifying circumstances under §15 appear, so the statute permits appointment to civil service.

steps: Verified citizenship: registry shows Estonian citizen (§14 requirement).
Verified education: registry shows at least secondary education (§14 requirement).
Verified legal capacity: registry indicates full capacity (§14 requirement).
Verified language: registry indicates proficiency in Estonian (§14 requirement).
Checked criminal disqualifiers: registry shows no criminal conviction (§15 disqualifier absent).
Checked nepotism/family conflict: applicant confirmed no family conflict with supervising official (§15(4) disqualification).
Noted that certain posts may impose additional, post-specific requirements set by law or the authority (§14(3), §10); those are not checked here.
justification.text: Authoritative registries show the applicant meets the baseline statutory requirements for employment in the civil service (citizenship, education, legal capacity, Estonian proficiency, no criminal disqualifier) and the applicant confirmed absence of a family conflict; appointment remains subject to any post-specific requirements and the normal selection procedure.

steps: Identify statutory eligibility: §14 permits Estonian citizens and EU Member State citizens who meet requirements; some sensitive posts reserved for Estonian citizens only.

Check citizenship in registry: population registry (authoritative) reports ee_citizen=true (contradicting applicant's self-report), which satisfies §14 requirements regardless (Estonian or EU citizen permitted).

Verify other statutory prerequisites from authoritative registries: secondary_education=true (meets §14(1)), speaks_estonian=true (language proficiency), full_capacity=true (active legal capacity), criminal_conviction=false (no prohibiting convictions per §15).

Check statutory prohibitions: no registry evidence of disqualifying criminal punishment or incapacity; applicant also self-confirms no family conflict with supervising official (no contrary registry data provided).
Conclusion: all statutory employment-in-service requirements and absence of disqualifying grounds are satisfied on the available authoritative records.
justification.text: Authoritative registries show the person has the required education, Estonian language proficiency, active legal capacity and no disqualifying criminal record, and citizenship recorded (Estonian) satisfies §14; no statutory prohibition under §15 appears, so employment in the service is permitted.

steps: Determine statutory eligibility: §14 allows employment of Estonian citizens (and EU citizens) who have at least secondary education, active legal capacity and required Estonian proficiency; §15 lists disqualifications (criminal convictions, certain family relations, etc.).

Applicant states they are a Georgian citizen (non-EE/non-EU) which would ordinarily bar appointment under §14, but authoritative population registry record indicates ee_citizen = true (contradicting applicant).

Authoritative education registry shows secondary_education = true, language registry shows speaks_estonian = true, population registry shows full_capacity = true, and criminal-records registry shows criminal_conviction = false — all meet the statutory requirements and no disqualifying conviction is recorded.
Applicant also affirmed no family conflict with a supervising official (no evidence to the contrary in supplied authoritative records).
On the basis of the authoritative registry data satisfying §14 and absence of disqualifying facts under §15, the appointment is permitted.
justification.text: Authoritative registries show the person is an Estonian citizen, has secondary education, required Estonian proficiency, active legal capacity and no criminal conviction, meeting the requirements of §14 and not triggering the disqualifications of §15, so the statute permits employment.

steps: Identify statutory requirements for employment in service (§14): Estonian citizenship, at least secondary education, active legal capacity, and proficiency in Estonian to the level required by law.

Check registry evidence: population registry (ee_citizen=true, full_capacity=true), education registry (secondary_education=true), language registry (speaks_estonian=true), criminal-records registry (criminal_conviction=false) — all authoritative.
Note applicant's self-report that they do not yet speak Estonian at required level conflicts with the authoritative language registry entry.
No prohibition under §15 is triggered by the records (no convictions, no family conflict with supervisor).
justification.text: Authoritative registry data show the applicant satisfies the statutory conditions of §14 (Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency) and §15 raises no disqualifying grounds, so the statute permits appointment.

steps: Verify statutory eligibility under §14: applicant is Estonian, has secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency — all satisfied according to registers and statement.

Check disqualifications in §15: persons “under punishment for an intentionally committed criminal offence” or punished for intentional offences against the state are barred; prior convictions per se are not categorically barred unless the person is currently under punishment or the offence is one against the state.

Compare factual records: criminal-records registry (authoritative, available) indicates no criminal_conviction; the applicant’s self-report of a conviction two years ago conflicts with the authoritative registry.

Because the registry is authoritative and no evidence was provided that the applicant is currently serving a punishment or was convicted of an offence against the state, no statutory bar under §15 is established for this applicant.
Conclusion: on the given information and authoritative records, the statutory requirements are met and no prohibition under §15 has been shown.
justification.text: Authoritative registry data show no criminal conviction and the applicant meets the §14 requirements; §15 only bars persons currently under punishment or those punished for offences against the state, neither of which is established here, so appointment is permissible.

steps: Check statutory minimums: §14 requires an Estonian citizen with at least secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency.
Verify available records: authoritative registries show secondary_education=true, speaks_estonian=true, and criminal_conviction=false — these satisfy education, language and absence of convictions.

Citizenship and active legal capacity appear only in a register entry with warrant='trust_only' (self-report), not an authoritative source; §14 requires those conditions but they are not authoritatively verified.
§15 disqualifies close-family relationships with a supervising official; the applicant self-confirms no family conflict but no authoritative verification is present.

Because required eligibility elements (citizenship, legal capacity) and the absence of prohibited family ties are missing or only self-reported, the statutory prerequisites cannot be reliably confirmed.
justification.text: Authoritative confirmation of Estonian citizenship and active legal capacity and verification that no disqualifying family relationship with a supervising official exists are required under §§14 and 15 but are only present as unverified self-report; obtain authoritative verification before permitting appointment.

steps: Identify statutory citizenship requirement for employment in service (§14): either Estonian citizen with secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency, or EU citizen who meets requirements.

Check registers: eu_citizen = false (authoritative) → applicant is not an EU citizen; secondary_education = true, full_capacity = true, speaks_estonian = true, criminal_conviction = false (all authoritative).
Conclude that if applicant is not an EU citizen, Estonian citizenship must be established to satisfy §14, but registers do not state Estonian citizenship.

Check §15 prohibition on employment of persons with certain family relationships to supervising officials; applicant self-confirms no family conflict but there is no authoritative verification in the provided records.
Because Estonian citizenship and verification of absence of prohibited familial ties to supervising officials are missing, statutory eligibility cannot be determined conclusively.
justification.text: Registries show education, legal capacity, Estonian proficiency and no criminal conviction, but the applicant is not an EU citizen and Estonian citizenship is not present in the records; additionally absence of prohibited family ties to supervising officials is only a self‑report and not verified.

steps: Applicant submitted application and a written confirmation of no family conflict with any supervising official (per §25(1)1).
§15(4) disqualifies persons who are close relatives of an official who has direct control over the post; absence of such relation must be ascertained for eligibility.
§14(1) requires an Estonian citizen with active legal capacity and §14(1) (and §25) requires Estonian proficiency and minimum education for employment in service.
Registry data: education_registry (secondary_education=true) and language_registry (speaks_estonian=true) are authoritative and available; criminal_records_registry shows no conviction.
Population registry (which would verify ee_citizen and full_capacity) is marked unavailable despite containing fields, so citizenship and legal capacity cannot be relied on from the payload.
No authoritative registry data about family relationships to supervising officials was provided, so the absence of a disqualifying family conflict cannot be verified.
justification.text: The applicant’s self-confirmation is noted, but statutory eligibility requires verification that no disqualifying family relation exists (§15(4)) and confirmation of Estonian citizenship and active legal capacity (§14); the population registry data needed for those checks is unavailable and no family-relationship data was provided.
